caption: I still grocery shop like there are two of us. Does that ever stop, or do you just get used to the leftovers?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R22 800
p/m salary
Living in Vanderbijlpark
slides.body:
Female, 52
Widow, living alone since last year
Job: HR clerk, ArcelorMittal
Net salary: R22 800 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.includes: The house we bought together, now paid by me alone
slides.body: It was always going to be my name eventually. I didn't expect it to be this soon.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Still driving his bakkie, couldn't bring myself to sell it
slides.body: I don't need it. I'm keeping it anyway.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.includes: Just my own plan now, downgraded from the family option
slides.body: The paperwork to change it took longer than I expected. Everything admin-related did.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Pick n Pay, still buying two of everything half the time
slides.body: I catch myself reaching for his brand of coffee most weeks.

slides.title: Funeral policy
slides.includes: Increased mine after his passing, added a small one for my son too
slides.body: Wasn't planning on thinking about this again so soon. Did it anyway.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, phone & fibre, petrol, a stokvel I kept up even this year, savings I've started again
slides.body: Rebuilding this part slowly. Some months better than others.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R22 800. On paper there's more room now than there used to be. It doesn't feel that way.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what the house actually costs alone
slides.body:
I uploaded a year of statements to Beyond Horizon to see what changed since it became just me.

Groceries barely dropped. Everything else did.

No bank login needed.
